Even out contrast in every image, tile by tile.

Contrast Limited Adaptive Histogram Equalization (OpenCV createCLAHE) on each tile of the image; colour images change only their lightness (Lab L), so colours stay, unless colour is each_channel. Clip limit caps how far contrast is raised. Done once when the images are prepared: OpenCV on the CPU workers, in canvas order with the other steps done once; every epoch reads the result. Same result in training, validation and test.

## Settings

| Setting | Key | Type | Default | Allowed values | Read by | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Clip limit | `clip_limit` | Number | `2.0` | `>0` | The run | How far contrast may be raised; 1 is almost none. |
| Tile grid (tiles per side) | `tile_grid` | Integer | `8` | `>0` | The run | Tiles per side; each tile gets its own histogram. |
| Colour images | `colour` | Choice | `lightness` | `lightness`, `each_channel` | The run | lightness: Lab L only, colours stay; each_channel: R, G and B alone. |

**Read by** says whether a run uses the setting (**The run**) or only the editor, a dialog or a view (**The editor only**).

## Usage

```text
Resize -> Image Contrast (CLAHE) -> Normalize -> Conv2D. Put it before the first random step (flips, crops, Rotate, Color Jitter).
```

```text
Done once when the images are prepared (OpenCV, CPU), in canvas order before the first random step. Runs in training, validation and test.
```

## Tips

- Dark or washed-out photos: details in shadows and highlights show.
- X-rays and scans: the usual first step.
